title: Orchid Labs pilot - prompt reuse and KV surge review
next_steps: SE to share updated hit-rate breakdown with per-route latency by 2026-06-29
Customer to provide canonical prompt variants CSV by 2026-06-28
Schedule final run of 24h traffic replay (Devon to approve)
action_items: Maya - send pricing impact sheet for KV hit rates > 65% by 2026-06-29
Ethan - run targeted cache eviction sim and share results by 2026-06-30
Rina - export top 200 prompt prefixes and upload to shared drive by 2026-06-28
header: Date: 2026-06-25 15:00 PDT; Duration: 42m; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Orchid ML), Carlos Gomez (Orchid Infra), Sofia Lim (Orchid Product), Devon Harris (Orchid CTO, joined 15:18)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on KV/prefix cache hit-rate variability and a new prompt-reuse signature approach. Team reviewed last 72h metrics, discussed two outlier routes driving cache churn, agreed on eviction tuning + canonical prompt mapping, and planned a 24h traffic replay to validate expected cost savings. Action items assigned.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: okay starting, hi everyone, thanks for joining — good to catch up on the pilot progress
00:08 Rina: hey — yes thanks, quick note we have a hard stop at 15:42 but should be fine
00:12 Ethan: cool, i'll kick us off with the dashboard highlights i shared earlier, sorry if some labels are off — fireflies auto export sometimes mangles the env names
00:21 Ethan: so top line, overall KV hit-rate averaged 58% over the last 72 hours, but there's a big variance by route, some routes at 82% and two at like under 30%
00:33 Carlos: yeah those two routes are our search-suggest and web-scrape-normalize — they have a lot of ephemeral prefixes
00:40 Maya: right and that ephemeral prefix churn is what causes eviction thrash, so we see the KV store turned over more frequently than the prefix cache expects
00:49 Rina: quick clarification — when you say prefix cache, are you distinguishing the prefix index vs the actual KV value cache? sometimes our team uses them interchangeably

00:56 Ethan: good point — in our charts prefix hit-rate is 'prefix match at request time' and KV hit-rate is 'found value in KV store after prefix match', so you can have prefix matches but still miss due to value eviction
01:10 Sofia: i noticed in the dashboard the latency spiked specifically on those low-hit routes — was that correlated to GPU cold starts or purely cache misses?

01:19 Ethan: mostly cache misses, the trace shows increased token generation time because requests fell back to full decode, not a GPU spin-up. There are some small tails attributable to batch packing but not the main cause

01:33 Rina: okay makes sense. we also ran a quick prompt-abstraction step on our side to group functionally equivalent prompts — results are in the shared sheet, link: drive.google.com/orchid/pilot/prefixsigs

01:47 Maya: awesome — that helps for prompt-reuse strategy. we noticed a lot of near-duplicates where only a date or a user id changed, so canonicalizing those should improve both prefix and KV hit rates
02:02 Carlos: question: if we canonicalize aggressively, are we risking QA/regression on outputs for custom prompts? we can't afford to collapse some templates that require exact phrasing

02:11 Ethan: there's a tradeoff — we propose a two-tier mapping: conservative canonicalization for critical routes (keep exact phrasing) and more aggressive for lower-risk routes; SE can produce a mapping table and confidence score
02:26 Rina: that sounds good. what about eviction policy — right now it's LRU with a 48h TTL for values, which seems too blunt
02:35 Ethan: yes LRU + fixed TTL is what you're on, we tested adaptive TTL based on prefix reuse frequency, that reduced churn by approx 12% in our sim

02:46 Maya: i pulled the sim results into the slides, link: drive.redwood/infer/pilot-sim-jun25 (note: internal link, shared with orchid), there we show an adaptive TTL that extends popular keys to 7d and shorter for low reuse
03:01 Sofia: was the sim run using real traffic distribution or uniform sampling?
03:07 Ethan: real distribution — we replayed 72 hours but bucketed routes and preserved interarrival times, we didn't do the 24h full replay yet, that's the next validation
03:15 Devon: (joined) sorry i'm late, quick high level — are we on track to hit the 65% KV threshold that the finance team asked for?
03:23 Maya: we are trending toward it if we combine prompt canonicalization and adaptive TTL plus targeted eviction for ephemeral prefixes — baseline 58% could go to ~70% in sim, depends on rollout
03:33 Devon: ok good. what about the cost model — how do those improvements translate to CPU/GPU token cost?

03:39 Ethan: short answer: every 10% increase in KV hit-rate reduces per-request token decode by roughly 0.7 tokens on average for your workload shape, that's approx 8-12% token cost reduction. we'll share a more precise per-route sheet
03:58 Carlos: is that modeled with the same batch sizes we see in prod? i.e., bursty web traffic not uniform throughput
04:06 Ethan: yes we used your observed burst distribution; caching benefits are slightly less in burst windows due to batch packing variability but still material
04:18 Rina: a weird observation — route A shows repeated cache churn at roughly 4am UTC, any idea?
04:24 Maya: could be a nightly job or indexer updating content that touches those keys; do you have a cron job?
04:29 Carlos: yes we run a metadata refresh at 03:55 UTC that reconstructs some entities — that explains the churn

04:35 Ethan: okay that explains the periodic eviction. options: shift the refresh window, mark keys as tombstoned to avoid rebuilding identical values, or make TTL extension resilient to background writes
04:46 Rina: marking tombstones might be complicated, prefer shifting maintenance off-peak, but we want a solution that doesn't require ops changes ideally
04:53 Maya: understood. another lever is prefix signature expansion — if your maintenance job preserves the same canonical signature we can keep hits despite background updates
05:02 Sofia: what's involved to get from our current prompt list to canonical signatures? Rina you said you prepared a CSV?
05:08 Rina: yes uploaded, file name: orchid_prefix_sigs_2026_06_25.csv — includes 1,200 unique variants mapped to 180 canonical signatures
05:16 Ethan: perfect. SE will ingest that and run a dry run to estimate hit-rate uplift. expected uplift in sim was ~9% at route level if mapping accuracy > 85%
05:27 Devon: any risk of mapping false positives — i mean collapsing two semantically different prompts into one signature?
05:33 Ethan: small risk, that's why the mapping tool returns a confidence score and we recommend a canary where we only remap high-confidence matches and log the others for manual review
05:45 Maya: ok let's talk schedule: Ethan, can you run the mapping ingestion and eviction sim and share updated charts by end of week?
05:54 Ethan: yes i can do that, target Thursday EOD PST (2026-06-29) — i'll include per-route latency impact and token delta
06:03 Maya: and Rina will upload the extended prompt variants and flag critical routes by Monday?
06:09 Rina: i can do Monday 6/28, yep
06:13 Carlos: on the 24h traffic replay — we need a governance checkbox from Devon to run it in your environment, Devon can you confirm?
06:20 Devon: yes i'll approve if SE provides a short runbook and rollback steps — concerned about stateful writes during replay
06:27 Ethan: for replay we'll use read-only sampling and replay against a staging read replica, no writes; will provide runbook and rollback notes
06:35 Sofia: perfect. one more small ask: can Redwood expose a per-request prefix score so our ops can triage low-hit sessions more easily?
06:44 Ethan: yes we can add a small tracing tag that surfaces prefix match confidence and whether KV value was returned. low overhead on the trace headers
06:52 Maya: i'll add that to the action items. all right let's pivot to a specific outlier route — Route X showed large variance and was driving most of the cost
07:01 Ethan: pulling up Route X, its prefix space is huge because user prompts include freeform urls — we suggested normalizing urls as part of canonicalization, strip query params, map known domains
07:12 Rina: stripping query params should be fine but we must keep path segments for some vendors, so the normalization rules need to be tunable per-domain
07:21 Ethan: agreed, we can parameterize normalizers per domain. SE will propose a rule set and a safe default fallback
07:30 Carlos: curious about the cache key size — we saw some keys get large and that affects eviction heuristics, is there a recommended max key length?
07:38 Ethan: practical recommendation is 512 bytes for key serialization; anything longer add a hashed fingerprint to avoid storing enormous keys
07:46 Rina: good to know, we'll review our serializer — we sometimes include full headers currently which bloats keys

07:52 Maya: okay we're 30 minutes in, quick recap from my side: 1) SE runs ingestion + eviction sim by 6/29, 2) Orchid uploads extended prompt CSV by 6/28, 3) Maya to send pricing model by 6/29, 4) agree canary approach then run 24h replay after Devon approval
08:12 Devon: thanks, and one ask from execs — if possible include a conservative upside and tail risk column in the results so we can present to finance
08:21 Ethan: will do, will include 5th/95th percentile outcomes for hit-rate and token cost
08:29 Sofia: can we also get a short doc on how to rollback the canonicalization if we see user-impact?
08:35 Maya: yes, SE will draft a rollback playbook and share with Orchid ops
08:41 Carlos: small note — our security team will want to review any new telemetry tagging, we'll loop them in once you have the tag spec
08:49 Maya: noted, add security review to the checklist
08:55 Rina: one last quick question — are there any Redwood product limits we should know for KV size or number of keys?

09:02 Ethan: current soft limits for the pilot: per-tenant KV namespace up to 20M keys in the Dedicated pilot settings and per-key value size up to 256KB, we'll share the limits doc, but can discuss enterprise adjustments
09:16 Maya: sharing link: redwood.docs/pilot-kv-limits — we'll send exact entitlement in follow-up
09:23 Devon: ok thanks everyone, i'm comfortable with the plan. let's reconvene after the sim results — tentative next sync Friday 6/30 same time
09:33 Maya: great, i'll schedule and send calendar invite. thanks all
09:36 Rina: thanks, bye
09:38 Ethan: thanks, bye
09:40 (call ends)
